brief: Goldman Sachs Morning note (Adam Crook, FX & Macro Sales) is structured as five sections: Connecting you to GS, Data Centre Forecasts, NZD Update, Latest FX Trader, and Week Ahead Previews. Only the first section's text was extracted; the other four are listed by title only with no body text captured. The extracted section relays GS Chief US Political Economist Alec Phillips's take on the US midterms' effect on the AI data-centre buildout: the biggest surprise was at the state level, not the federal level. Federally, Phillips expects data-centre-focused policy but nothing extreme, ratepayer protections and possibly removing some existing tax incentives. At the state level, gubernatorial wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio put, in theory, up to around 40% of planned data-centre capacity at risk from permitting moratoria, and Phillips expects a temporary moratorium lasting several months until new rules are set. Pre-election, markets priced about a 65% chance Texas Governor Abbott would win re-election.
